identity.name: MEGADOCK CPU/GPU docking pilot on four PINDER 2024-02 apo cases

outcome_definition.execution_acceleration: Trusted invocation wall for CPU and GPU at identical settings.
outcome_definition.scientific_agreement: Compare ranked transforms, scores and model coordinates for A0 and A1; numerical acceptance criterion unavailable.
outcome_definition.pose_recovery: DockQ for top-ranked pose and best of 50 separately, for each case and arm; denser GPU search changes only rotational sampling.
outcome_definition.scope: Four-case pilot; no inference of biological efficacy.

outputs.name: transforms
outputs.what: The rotation and translation fields of every ranked prediction row of the arm's docking.out (all fields of the row except the last), in file order.

outputs.name: scores
outputs.what: The score field (the last field) of every ranked prediction row of the arm's docking.out, in file order.

outputs.name: coords
outputs.what: The x, y and z coordinate columns of every ATOM and HETATM record of the arm's assembled models, models taken in rank order.

outputs.name: dockq
outputs.what: The evaluator's DockQ value for each of the arm's assembled models, as one JSON array in rank order, in a file that holds no other number.

metrics.name: wall
metrics.what: Trusted wall of the invocation: adapter and arm commands, plus the evaluator part.

metrics.name: dockq_rank1
metrics.what: The evaluator's DockQ value of the arm's top-ranked model for the input: the first value of the evaluator's DockQ array.

metrics.name: dockq_best50
metrics.what: The largest of the evaluator's DockQ values over all of the arm's retained models for the input.

scoring.reason: Brief explicitly states no published anchors for these inputs. Neither source hashes nor generated checks are scientific anchors.

repeatability.seed_reason: No randomized seed supplied for deterministic rotational search.
rules: Use exactly the four sealed inputs and all three fixed arms; no scale search.
Preserve each invocation, failure and timeout; no reruns outside the pipeline schedule.
Pipeline alone compares outputs and reduces DockQ metrics; no adapter or evaluator comparison or summary.
Reference structures only available to evaluator.
repeatability.agreement_tolerances_reason: No published or sealed numerical agreement criterion supplied; do not invent one.

A1.what: Seed configuration 2: the published MEGADOCK GPU build with the same sampling and scientific settings as A0, followed by the same reconstruction and assembly as A0.
commands: set -euo pipefail; for r in $(seq 1 50); do baseline-published/megadock/decoygen "lig_$r.pdb" "$2" "$0/docking.out" "$r" > "decoygen_$r.log" 2>&1; grep -v '^END' "$1" > "$0/model_$r.pdb"; grep -v -E '^(END|ENDMDL)' "lig_$r.pdb" >> "$0/model_$r.pdb"; echo END >> "$0/model_$r.pdb"; done

A2.what: Seed configuration 3: the published MEGADOCK GPU build with MEGADOCK's documented denser rotational sampling (its -D option) in place of the standard rotation set, all other scientific settings as in A1, followed by the same reconstruction and assembly as A0.
commands: set -euo pipefail; for r in $(seq 1 50); do baseline-published/megadock/decoygen "lig_$r.pdb" "$2" "$0/docking.out" "$r" > "decoygen_$r.log" 2>&1; grep -v '^END' "$1" > "$0/model_$r.pdb"; grep -v -E '^(END|ENDMDL)' "lig_$r.pdb" >> "$0/model_$r.pdb"; echo END >> "$0/model_$r.pdb"; done

evaluator.command_unavailable_reason: The comparison view publishes an API invocation contract, not a standalone executable evaluator command; evaluate.sh and its embedded Python program are to be authored downstream. No command is invented here.
evaluator.invocation: BiotiteDockQ is constructed with parallel_io=False (models read in the evaluator's own process). evaluate.sh is self-contained: it carries the evaluator's Python program in its own text, writes it at each call to a regular file under CMP_EVAL_OUT, and runs it as the venv interpreter followed by that file's path. It never runs a program read from standard input (PINDER's parallel reader starts its workers with the spawn method, which re-imports the main program from its file) and never runs or reads any other file under harness/, which is not uploaded to the box.

spec.private_data: for each input, the native complex named in spec.reference, fetched by fetch_private.sh from its URL and checked against its SHA-256 (the concatenation of the pieces in spec.reference.sha256) and byte count. fetch_private.sh is self-contained: it carries each input's reference name, URL, byte count and SHA-256 in its own text and reads no other file under harness/, because only the sealed comparison files and the usual harness scripts are uploaded to the box.
spec.reads: the model_<rank>.pdb files under CMP_ARM_OUT, in rank order; the native complex under CMP_PRIVATE at the name, byte count and SHA-256 (the concatenation of the pieces) given by spec.reference in CMP_INPUT_SPEC
spec.invocation: BiotiteDockQ is constructed with parallel_io=False (models read in the evaluator's own process). evaluate.sh is self-contained: it carries the evaluator's Python program in its own text, writes it at each call to a regular file under CMP_EVAL_OUT, and runs it as the venv interpreter followed by that file's path. It never runs a program read from standard input (PINDER's parallel reader starts its workers with the spawn method, which re-imports the main program from its file) and never runs or reads any other file under harness/, which is not uploaded to the box.
spec.writes: CMP_EVAL_OUT/dockq.json, one JSON array of the DockQ values in rank order and no other number; any per-model detail goes to a separate file under CMP_EVAL_OUT

evaluator.installation_commands:
python3 -m venv --system-site-packages "$VENV"
"$VPY" -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade "setuptools>=64" "setuptools_scm>=8" packaging wheel 2>&1 \
  | tee "$SOUT/pip_install_build_tools.log"
SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION="$PINDER_SCM_VERSION" SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PINDER="$PINDER_SCM_VERSION" \
  "$VPY" -m pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation "$WORK/$BP/pinder-src" 2>&1 | tee "$SOUT/pip_install_pinder.log"
"$VPY" -m pip install --no-cache-dir fire 2>&1 | tee "$SOUT/pip_install_fire.log"
printf 'numpy<2\n' > "$SOUT/venv_constraints.txt"
"$VPY" -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade -c "$SOUT/venv_constraints.txt" networkx pandas scikit-learn 2>&1 \
  | tee "$SOUT/pip_install_venv_refresh.log"
